one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban shares a summary of the speech he delivered on Nov 16 when the Rotary Club of Manila -- joined by several Rotarians from other clubs -- honored him as 'the Only Philippine Rotary President to Become Chief Justice,' at the invitation of district governor-elect Jackie Rodriguez. He situates RCM as the first and oldest Rotary club in Asia (founded June 1, 1919), and recalls that during his 1990-1991 presidency it had 455 members -- the largest in the world outside the United States -- composed of Cabinet members, senators, congressmen, justices, 40 doctors, 50 lawyers, bank presidents, ambassadors, and heads of the country's top 300 companies, meeting at the Manila Hotel, with Presidents Marcos Sr., Cory Aquino, and Fidel V. Ramos using the RCM rostrum for major national messages. Under RCM's unique rule that the board's top vote-getter automatically became president, his name was put forward in 1989; he asked his Bukas Loob sa Diyos (BLD) Catholic charismatic group to discern with him through scripture, and they were led to Isaiah 42:1-8 ('Here is my servant whom I uphold...'). He won by a record margin in December 1989 and used the seven months before his July 1990 induction to plan. Further BLD prayer led to Mark 12:29-32, the Lord's two-commandment summary, from which he distilled the credo 'LOVE GOD SERVE MAN.' He expanded this into a 76-page printed Program of Action -- a 'first' in RCM's history -- with 178 projects, specific timelines, and a P90-million budget (eighteen times the prior P5-million annual outlay). His July 12, 1990 inaugural invoked Matthew 25's 'least of our brothers'; reactions ranged from 'Why is religion now a program of RCM?' to 'Alleluia, what a spirit-filled speech!' The true test came four days after induction, when the July 16, 1990 Baguio killer earthquake (magnitude 7.7, 2,000+ deaths) struck. At the July 19 RCM meeting, he pleaded for assistance and members responded with P7 million cash -- sixteen times his best expectations -- plus medical missions, product donations, clothes and groceries, a 'tent city' for 250 families in Burnham Park, and a 3,300-kilo single airlift from the Rotary Club of Waikiki. He read the response as Providence's answer to the credo. A year later, on June 27, 1991, he delivered his valedictory with a 94-page printed Final Report showing 95 percent of the program accomplished and a roadmap for the remaining 5 percent.
